parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The slew rate of an ideal operational amplifier (op-amp) is said to be infinite.
Explain what is meant by infinite slew rate.

markscheme_points.text: there is no time delay between change in input and change in output
or reference to rate at which output voltage changes (B1) infinite rate of change (of output voltage)

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in operational amplifiers that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: reference to input (voltage) and output (voltage); there is no time delay between change in input and change in output; or reference to rate at which output voltage changes (B1) infinite rate of change (of output voltage)
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Operational amplifiers. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Apply Physics Criteria**
Explain the mechanism clearly using standard terminology:
reference to input (voltage) and output (voltage); there is no time delay between change in input and change in output; or reference to rate at which output voltage changes (B1) infinite rate of change (of output voltage)

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Determine the resistance of resistor R such that the output $V_{\mathrm{OUT}}$ of the op-amp changes
at 24 °C.
$resistance = Ω $
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in operational amplifiers connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Operational amplifiers. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
2.00 / 3.00 = 1.50 / R; or V+ = (3.00 × 4.5) / (2.00 + 3.00) = 2.7 2.7 = 4.5 × R / (R + 1.50) (C1) resistance = 2.25 kΩ
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 6.1,
1.
draw two light-emitting diodes (LEDs) connected so as to indicate whether the
output $V_{\mathrm{OUT}}$ of the op-amp is either +5 V or −5 V,
2.
label with the letter G the LED that will be emitting light when the temperature is
below 24 °C. Explain your working.

markscheme_points.text: two LEDs connected with opposite polarities between VOUT and earth
2. below 24 °C, RT > 1.5 kΩ or resistance of thermistor increases/high
V- < V+ or V- decreases/low (must not contradict initial statement)
VOUT is positive/+5 (V) and LED labelled as ‘pointing’ from VOUT to earth

hints: Hint 1: Draw the circuit showing two LEDs connected in parallel with opposite polarities between $V_{OUT}$ and earth.
Hint 2: Explain how the resistance of the thermistor changes when temperature falls below $24^{\circ}\text{C}$.
Hint 3: Use potential divider reasoning to determine how the inverting potential $V_-$ compares to the non-inverting potential $V_+$.
Hint 4: Deduce the output state: since $V_- < V_+$, the op-amp output saturates at positive voltage ($+5\text{ V}$).
Hint 5: Identify which LED has its anode connected to $V_{OUT}$ and cathode to earth, and will therefore be forward-biased and emit light.
parts.proper_answer: 1. correct symbol for LED; two LEDs connected with opposite polarities between VOUT and earth; 2. below 24 °C, RT > 1.5 kΩ or resistance of thermistor increases/high; V- < V+ or V- decreases/low (must not contradict initial statement); VOUT is positive/+5 (V) and LED labelled as ‘pointing’ from VOUT to earth
walkthrough:

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**

Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
